info.title: Epora permission wallet API
info.description:
HTTP access to the Epora permission wallet: read its indexed on-chain state, and
build transactions against its smart contracts.

**The server never holds a key and never signs.** Every `/api/v1/tx/*` route takes an
address, returns an unsigned transaction as CBOR hex, and leaves signing and submission
to the caller.

**Network.** Preprod only. Addresses must be `addr_test1...`.

**Versioning.** `v1` describes the current shape of the API. The compatibility promise
starts at the mainnet beta: until then a `v1` route may change without a version bump,
and this document is the record of what it does today. After the beta, breaking changes
get a new version prefix.

**Errors.** Every failure returns the same body, `{ "error": "..." }`. A `400` carries a
message naming what to fix. A `502` means the chain data provider is unreachable, and
never carries the provider's own text.

**Rate limits.** Per client address: 5 requests per
60s across all transaction builds together,
60 per 60s for wallet lookups,
30 per 60s for pool lookups. Builds also
share a deployment-wide cap of 25 per
60s, because one build costs the chain provider tens of
requests. Every `429` carries `Retry-After`. Deployments may set their own caps.

See [the developer guide](https://github.com/schaier-io/epora-wallet/blob/main/docs/api/README.md).

tags.name: Transactions
tags.description: Build unsigned transactions. The caller signs them.

get.description: Returns 200 when the app can reach its database, and 503 when it cannot, so an uptime monitor can alert on the difference. Deliberately unversioned: a health probe is operational, not part of the public contract.

503.description: The service is up but a dependency is down.

get.description: Fetch one stake pool's details and metadata by id.

schema.description: Stake pool id, either bech32 `pool1...` or a 56-character hex id.

fields.description: The constructor's fields, in declaration order.

ConstrData.description: A Plutus constructor value: an alternative index and its fields. Byte strings are hex, integers are JSON numbers, and nested constructors use this same shape.

unit.description: `lovelace`, or a policy id concatenated with a hex asset name.

assets.description: Value to deposit. At least one asset is required.

inlineDatum.description: Optional inline datum to attach to the deposit output.
